ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, beneficial owners, directors, managers, authorized signatories, and any third-party agent or nominee against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Consolidated Sanctions List; (iv) the United Kingdom HM Treasury Sanctions List; (v) the Luxembourg national list of persons and entities subject to financial restrictive measures under the Law of 19 December 2020; and (vi) the global sanctions and enforcement screening databases used by Luxembourg credit institutions. PEP status is assessed at initiation, at each major transaction, and at least annually, in accordance with Article 3 of the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, applying enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior-management approval whenever a PEP, family member, or known close associate is identified. Negative news and integrity searches are mandatory for all UBOs and managers before signing the notarial deed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the online filing of the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be submitted in Latin script and comply with the technical character set of the RCS information system. Official filing languages are French and German, and the name may be registered in either; names originating in non-Latin scripts (including Chinese, Cyrillic, or Arabic) must be transliterated into Latin characters and may be registered exclusively in that transliterated form. The legal name of the SARL must contain the designation 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the recognized abbreviations 'S.à r.l.' or 'SARL'. The name must be distinctive, not misleading, not contrary to public order or public morality, and clearly distinguishable from all prior corporate names, trademarks, and protected designations recorded at the RCS or with the Luxembourg intellectual property administration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed name by the RCS, the applicant may issue a request for written reasons from the RCS within five working days of the rejection notice. The applicant may then submit a revised name or names electronically through the LBR portal without loss of formal priority. If the rejection is maintained on grounds of conflict with an existing name, trademark, or protected designation, the applicant may file an administrative appeal addressed to the Minister of Justice under the Law of 19 December 2002 concerning the Register of Commerce and Companies, attaching the RCS rejection decision and documented argument on distinctiveness and non-confusion. A further judicial appeal lies with the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, siégeant en matière commerciale, and must be introduced by written petition (requête) within one month of notification of the final rejection. Names rejected solely because a token appears on the prohibited list may be cured without further review if the token is removed or if the prior ministerial authorization of the competent supervisory ministry is obtained. A name reserved under a valid RCS non-use certificate lapses after 40 days where the notarial deed has not been filed; a renewed reservation request is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible in Luxembourg solely for the statutory registered seat (siège statutaire), administrative correspondence, and records filing, provided the address provider is a supervised entity such as a licensed fiduciary, trust company, or registered company service provider. The virtual seat cannot, however, satisfy the real commercial substance requirements applicable to an active manufacturer and distributor of Class IIb/III medical devices. Under Luxembourg tax administration Circular L.I.R. n. 14/4 on profit attribution and substance, a mere letterbox or virtual-office seat, without effective management, staff, premises, and decision-making, creates a rebuttable presumption of non-residence for corporate tax purposes. For the present ISIC 3250 endoscope tower manufacturing and distribution activity, the Luxembourg operational functions — including CE marking vigilance obligations under Regulation (EU) 2017/745, post-market surveillance, quality management system records, import/export documentation, and authorized representative duties — require a physical establishment in the Grand Duchy with dedicated personnel and servers. The virtual office is therefore conditionally permissible for the statutory seat during the pre-incorporation and licensing phase, but a fully equipped physical office must be established before the first commercial invoice is issued.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 12.5% quantified probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 18 months of incorporation, reflective of the low-risk AML/CFT manufacturing profile but elevated by the medical-device regulatory perimeter. The probability increases to 25% where a virtual or shared office is used, where the value-added tax registration threshold is exceeded, or where the company maintains significant intra-group invoicing, imports, or customs activity. Unannounced inspections may be performed by the Luxembourg tax administration (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA - AEDT), the social inspection authority (Inspection du Travail et des Mines - ITM), and, specifically for medical devices, the Ministry of Health or the Luxembourg competent authority in medical technology surveillance pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2017/745.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg Inland Revenue) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax, and withholding taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT, registration duties, stamp duties, and excise tax administration; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for commercial registration and the national business identity number; all filings are supported by the Guichet.lu and e-Space digital portals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Luxembourg SARL must be incorporated by notarial deed, registered with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés. The RCS registration automatically generates the 13-digit Luxembourg business identification number ('matricule'). For VAT purposes, the entity must then file Form 810 (identification for VAT) with the AED, submitting the articles of association, notarised proof of incorporation, RCS excerpt, Luxembourg registered office evidence, identity documents of all managers and shareholders, certified copy of the corporate bank account statement, and, where applicable, valid audited financial statements or parent company details for group coordination. Non-resident suppliers established outside Luxembourg but making taxable transactions in Luxembourg must register directly with the AED using Form 810-A, appoint a tax representative when prescribed, and receive a LU VAT number under Article 15 of the Simplified VAT Collection Act; registration is mandatory prior to first taxable supply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a resident SARL is a corporate tax subject with full legal personality, taxed on its worldwide income unless treaty or EU law relief applies; non-resident entities are taxable only on Luxembourg-source income and assets. There is no transparent pass-through assessment for an SARL, and the entity is separately subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax, and VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; tax classification follows the statutory commercial legal form. Available elections include: (i) VAT fiscal unity ('assujetti unique') under Article 61 of the Luxembourg VAT Law for closely linked established taxable persons; (ii) non-Union OSS / Union OSS registration for cross-border B2C services and distance sales; (iii) optional application of the Luxembourg intellectual property box regime under Article 50ter of the Income Tax Law; (iv) an election for the small business VAT exemption to be waived; and (v) elections related to tax consolidation for VAT only. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are not elective; they are mandatorily adjusted under the Luxembourg provisions transposing EU ATAD, with no subjective check-the-box relief.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For non-resident suppliers making taxable supplies in Luxembourg, the registration threshold is 0 EUR; a VAT registration is mandatory before the first taxable transaction, regardless of turnover. For resident small enterprises, Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law grants an exemption where annual turnover, excluding VAT, does not exceed 25,000 EUR; the threshold applies to the preceding calendar year, and the enterprise may elect to register and charge VAT. Distance sales of goods by businesses established in another EU Member State to Luxembourg private consumers become taxable in Luxembourg only when the annual pan-EU distance-sales turnover exceeds the general EU threshold of 10,000 EUR, unless an OSS election is made.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently operate a real-time fiscal clearance or pre-clearance API for B2B invoices, and there is no digital stamping requirement. Taxpayers must submit periodic VAT returns, recapitulative statements, Intrastat declarations, and SAF-T/TLOG files through the AED's e-Space portal. All invoices issued for taxable supplies must comply with the VAT invoice content requirements under Articles 106-109 of the Luxembourg VAT Law. Traders issuing cash receipts for retail activities must use approved, tax-monitored electronic cash registers (eCDF/TLOG-compliant devices) that maintain a verifiable audit trail. For public-sector contracting, suppliers must transmit electronic invoices in the European standard EN 16931 through the Luxembourg BISON/PEPPOL interoperability network; B2B clearance is governed by EU ViDA transitional rules and is not yet active.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT export rate applies to supplies of goods dispatched or transported to a third country or third-territory destination, provided the goods physically leave the EU by the supplier, the customer, or a third party instructed by the supplier, within the statutory time frame (generally three months from the supply date, subject to extension on justifiable grounds). The supplier must hold documentary proof of the export, including a customs export declaration accepted by the competent customs office and evidence of the goods' actual exit from the EU. Export-related ancillary supplies, such as freight, packing, insurance, and inspection services directly related to the exported goods, are also zero-rated when included in the same export chain. Services rendered to non-EU customers are generally zero-rated where the customer is a taxable person established outside the EU, or where the effective place of use and enjoyment lies outside the EU for private consumers. Intra-EU supplies of medical devices to EU taxable persons are not 'exports' but are treated as zero-rated intra-Community supplies contingent on the customer's valid UK? — in Luxembourg context, a valid EU VAT identification number and submission of an EC sales list.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (AES export record / Single Administrative Document with exit confirmation) validated by Luxembourg or EU Customs
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing transport to the non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit entry evidencing receipt of foreign currency from the overseas buyer
Commercial invoice with Incoterms, HS tariff classification, unit value, and export destination
Packing list and transport insurance certificate, where applicable
Proof of the exporter's identity and entitlement to zero-rating (valid VAT registration and exporter code)
If applicable, the customer's non-EU status documentation or statutory declaration for exported services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg's AED applies strict documentary scrutiny to export zero-rating claims; if the export evidence is absent or defective within the statutory retention period, the VAT initially zero-rated is clawed back at 17% with statutory late-payment interest and late-filing surcharges. Administrative penalties may reach 100% of the tax evaded where the exporter knowingly issued a false export declaration, presented counterfeit transport documents, or artificially arranged an export transaction without an actual physical removal of goods. Criminal sanctions for fraud include fines of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment for up to five years for responsible officers, with possible disqualification of directors. Retrospective assessments are permitted for five years normally, extending to ten years in the presence of fraud or wilful concealment. The managing directors, fiscal representative, and, in limited cases, the general commercial agent are jointly and severally liable for the unrecovered VAT, interest, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem under the ultimate monetary authority of the European Central Bank (ECB). Luxembourg maintains no separate national foreign exchange administration; exchange control and monetary policy competences are pooled at the ECB level, with the BCL executing operations and supervising Luxembourg-licensed credit institutions within the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted Euro convertibility as a Eurozone member state. Luxembourg applies no exchange controls to either current or capital account transactions, consistent with Articles 63–66 TFEU on the free movement of capital. Profit remittance is freely executable via TARGET2/SEPA without FX licensing, but a standard statutory 15% Luxembourg withholding tax applies to dividends unless reduced or eliminated under an applicable double tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (0% for qualifying EU corporate shareholders). The practical remittance hurdle is purely documentary: banks require evidence of dividend approval, UBO disclosure, and corporate capacity, not FX authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg law imposes no statutory repatriation deadline and no mandatory EUR conversion ratio for export proceeds. Exporters may retain foreign-currency receivables in domiciled or foreign currency accounts indefinitely. Only CSSF AML/CFT reporting thresholds apply to large cross-border movements; medtech exporters invoicing in USD or CNY therefore enjoy complete treasury flexibility.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational payment flows, Low for statutory capital escrow. EU-licensed cross-border electronic money institutions may passport payment services into Luxembourg, but they cannot hold the SARL's registered capital in a blocked deposit account because deposit-taking and escrow of share capital are reserved to credit institutions under the Luxembourg law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector, as amended. Non-EU offshore EMIs without CSSF/EU authorization are not viable for corporate treasury. Practical recommendation: maintain the primary and escrow accounts at a Tier-1 bank and use fintech rails only for auxiliary disbursements, supplier payouts, or card programs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person appearance is the de facto norm for newly incorporated SARLs with non-resident shareholders. Luxembourg Tier-1 banks generally require at least one physical interview of the statutory manager (gérant) or a designated authorized signatory at the bank's Luxembourg premises. Remote opening is legally permissible under CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF Regulation 20-05 via video identification accompanied by ABA-compliant procedures, but most banks retain a discretionary additional in-person step where the ultimate beneficial owner is an offshore entity. A notarized special power of attorney can allow a Luxembourg-based professional director or counsel to attend the interview on behalf of overseas principals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain obscured by layered intermediate entities (e.g., a BVI or Delaware holding company above the SARL)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Linear ownership chart from ultimate individual to SARL; Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) attestation; notarized statutes of the SARL; constitutional documents and corporate resolutions of every intermediate entity; sworn source-of-wealth statement of each UBO; legal opinion from the jurisdictions in the chain confirming the absence of bearer shares and nominee ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection sourced from a high-risk or low-transparency jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letter from a top-tier international credit institution in the originator's jurisdiction; certified source-of-funds declaration; audited financial statements or tax returns of the transferring entity; signed undertaking describing the corporate purpose (manufacture and export of surgical laparoscopy towers under ISIC 3250); evidence that the injection constitutes equity, not a repayment obligation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or politically exposed person status of an ultimate beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Explicit PEP declaration on the standard CSSF form; explanation of the legitimate business rationale for the medical-device manufacturing investment; enhanced due diligence package including independent professional references, sanctions screening outputs, and third-party legal confirmation of the origin of wealth; commitment to ongoing PEP monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared manufacturing activity and the expected payment flows (Luxembourg is a holding/fund jurisdiction by default)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Manufacture authorization and CE-marking documentation for ultra-HD 4K rigid endoscopes; commercial contracts, purchase orders, and proforma invoices with distributors; proof of the Luxembourg siège social and registered office; payroll and social security filings confirming substance; CSSF-compliant board minutes directing treasury operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax residency ambiguity over the management seat (siège de direction)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg tax residency certificate (modèle 6); minutes of board meetings physically held in Luxembourg; director service agreements; social security registrations in Luxembourg; evidence that strategic procurement, treasury, and trade-finance decisions are made in Luxembourg; confirmation that no foreign permanent establishment has been created.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: (1) the SARL's minimum share capital (EUR 12,000) is transferred by SWIFT MT103 or via EU bank-to-bank TARGET2/T2 payment into a blocked capital account (compte bloqué) at a Luxembourg credit institution before notarial incorporation; (2) the transfer narrative must state the ECB/BPM6 balance-of-payments purpose code K7ED (equity other than reinvestment of earnings) and identify the SARL by IBAN (LU + national check digits) and the bank BIC; (3) the notary certifies the subscription and the blocked funds are released following the filing with the Luxembourg Trade Registry (RCS/LBR) and publication requirements; (4) documentary verification includes the preliminary notarial deed, the subscription forms, the board resolution designating the account, and the RBE/UBO declaration; (5) subsequent capital increases must follow the same blocked-account protocol with a notarized shareholders' resolution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 (serial or cover payment) for high-value USD and EUR trade settlements to overseas distributors and component suppliers; (b) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for EU-denominated payments, the latter capped at EUR 100,000 per transaction; (c) documentary commercial letters of credit (MT700) as the standard secure rail for export of surgical laparoscopy towers to Asia-Pacific and Middle Eastern buyers, with presentation of bills of lading, commercial invoices, packing lists, and certificates of origin; (d) standby letters of credit (MT760) as performance, advance-payment, and warranty guarantees; (e) bank payment undertakings or forfaiting desks may discount confirmed LC receivables to compress DSO. All outbound disbursements require bank-compliant supporting documentation (order, invoice, shipment evidence) and an economic-substance justification in the transfer narrative.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD FX forward contracts (plain-vanilla, physically settled)
EUR/JPY and EUR/SGD FX forward contracts for Asian component purchases
FX swaps and rolling outright forwards executed under bank ISDA/CK agreements
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for long-term USD receivables or intercompany loan hedging
European-style FX options (fully covered, physically settled) with a CSSF-regulated credit institution

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to restricted currencies (e.g., CNY, INR) booked via a Luxembourg credit institution or its licensed affiliate, where onshore deliverability is legally unavailable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, annex) of the SARL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) via eCDF electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the close of the financial year; annual shareholders' approval must occur within 6 months of the balance sheet date (calendar-year entities: approval by 30 June, filing by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Courts may order filing under an astreinte (per-diem penalty) after action by the Ministère Public; habitual or persistent non-filing exposes the SARL to administrative strike-off (radiation d'office) from the RCS and criminal fines for directors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owner information (confirmation annuelle RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs — RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year, due by 31 December; any change in beneficial ownership, including a share transfer creating a beneficial owner change, must be filed within 1 month of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal liability with fines ranging from €250 to €250,000 and/or imprisonment from 6 months to 5 years; AML/CFT supervisory measures may be imposed in parallel

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Unified corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax return for the SARL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg direct tax administration (Administration des contributions directes — ACD) via eTax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, no later than 31 December of the year following the tax year for calendar-year companies; extended deadlines may be granted by ACD on reasoned request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Ministry-regulated tax penalty up to €25,000 for late filing; statutory default interest is assessed on any overdue tax balance; prolonged non-compliance may trigger enforcement recovery and managing director personal liability for wilful default

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) is required when the SARL exceeds two of the following three criteria in two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total above €4.4 million, net turnover above €8.8 million, and average headcount above 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP derived from the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial companies and EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted by the EU applies to consolidated accounts of EU-listed groups and may be voluntarily elected for the parent entity accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each calendar year the SARL must file an annual confirmation through the RBE portal validating all beneficial owners and controlling interests. A share transfer resulting in a new beneficial owner is an intermediate filing event that must be reported to the RBE within one month of the transfer. The company secretary must reconcile the RBE profile with the shareholder register and file a mark-to-market update before the annual confirmation is accepted.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,300 – US$2,700 typical annual corporate agent and registered office fees in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$8,000 – US$15,000 for a typical medium-sized SARL in medical-device manufacturing subject to the statutory audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined headline rate (Luxembourg City basis): 17% corporate income tax (IRC, LIR Art. 174) + 1.19% solidarity surcharge (7% of IRC) + 6.75% municipal business tax (ICC). Progressive IRC scale applies below EUR 200,000 taxable income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Modified nexus-compliant IP box (LIR Art. 50bis): 80% deduction of net qualifying IP income, effective rate approx. 4.99%. 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends (>=10% holding or acquisition cost >=EUR 1.2M; 12-month holding; subsidiary subject to comparable tax) and on capital gains (>=10% or acquisition cost >=EUR 6M; LIR Art. 166). Refundable R&D tax credit (40% on first EUR 250,000 eligible R&D, 20% beyond, annual cap) and additional investment tax credit (8%) applicable to the endoscope manufacturing R&D activity.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carryforward under LIR Art. 114; no carryback permitted; forfeited if taxpayer ceases to be subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax).
